A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Matter-of-Fact benchmark. Their complete main texts, four tables, three figures, and Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, expert validation of 100 claims, and a model-contamination analysis in Sections 3–5 and Tables 2–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports a qualitative finding from an iterative retrieval pilot in Section 5.2.

M1.justification: v2 Section 5.2 newly describes an implemented retrieval pilot that gathers evidence iteratively through different queries before assessing feasibility. This adds a procedural variant to v1's single-query retrieval; benchmark construction and the main baseline pipelines remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 8.4K claims across superconductors, semiconductors, batteries, and aerospace materials, with the same feasibility-assessment and oracle claim-verification tasks. No additional dataset, domain, or task scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds a qualitative comparison involving an iterative retrieval pilot beyond the existing single-query baseline. The named models and comparator rows in Tables 2–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The newly reported pilot permits up to five evidence-collection rounds, each with a different query. Existing temporal splits, accuracy metrics, 20-shot examples, top-20 retrieval, and single-iteration, 10-minute code-execution settings are unchanged. The pilot's model and sample size are unspecified.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds a limited pilot testing whether iterative, multi-query evidence collection improves feasibility assessment. The contamination analysis in Table 4 and the hypothesis-filtering analysis in Appendix A are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same interrater-agreement reporting, including Cohen's kappa of 0.86. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new pilot has no statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports that the iterative retrieval pilot did not appear to improve feasibility performance, without numerical scores. Accuracy and cost entries in Tables 2–4, including the 0.72 maximum feasibility accuracy, and Appendix A's efficiency findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised. Backtesting names the existing temporal construction, and Appendix A's hypothetical filtering-efficiency reasoning is unchanged.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution, baseline-performance claims, validation claims, and hypothesis-filtering motivation are retained. The abstract now explicitly mentions temporally filtered verification using backtesting, which v1 already described in the introduction.

C2.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 substantially broaden the limitations beyond v1's contamination, ceiling-performance, and cost discussion. v2 identifies possible transfer problems from polished published claims, limitations of single-query evidence collection, and the restricted interpretation of code results without debugging or materials-specific tooling.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 now explicitly advertises the claim-extraction system alongside the benchmark and models. Section 5.2 newly discloses that CodeScientist's retrieval library lacked materials-specific tooling. These are additional access and implementation disclosures, without evidence that the main experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Huang et al. (2025), listed as Biomni in the references, to motivate integration of domain tools. The CodeScientist reference changes from preprint to conference publication, representing the same work. The broader related-work positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds backtesting terminology, organizes the discussion into two subsections, renames the cost-benefit limitations paragraph, expands acknowledgments, and corrects several spelling errors. Rewriting and reorganization are localized.

P2.justification: The existing figures and tables retain their content and visual designs. There are minor spacing and placement changes as text reflows, including relocation of Appendix A and Figure 3 from pages 11–12 to pages 12–13.

improvement.justification: v2 improves interpretation by explicitly addressing transfer from published claims to real discovery and explaining the baseline systems' limitations. Additional implementation and access disclosures also help. The gains remain limited: the main quantitative evidence and Appendix A are unchanged, and the retrieval pilot lacks scores and sufficient evaluation details.
